messages:
sana: Heads-up — spotted steady mem growth on canary after the kv-prefetch change. Heap diff shows ~120MB / host after ~10k long-conversation requests. Not typical.
liam: ugh. Is it due to prefix caching keeping more entries alive? any sample traces? :thinking_face:
josh: I grabbed a flamegraph and a small reproducer. Looks like we never evict some large prefix entries because their cache keys include ephemeral session tokens. Will paste logs.
sana: here's the minimal reproducer command I used: `wrk -t4 -c200 -d3m --latency http://canary.infer/stream?model=redwood-13b` with a long ctx prompt generator that shares initial 1k tokens across sessions.
josh: dump snippet of the key generation that caused it:
```
// bad: we included session metadata in key
string key = fmt::format("{}::sess={}", prefix_hash, session_id);
cache.put(key, kv_blob);
```
We were relying on session stickiness to coalesce, but the session_id made the same prefix look unique across sessions so cache blowup.
eva: oh wow. so reuse rate went down and fragmentation increased. did we also keep TTL infinite for these entries? that would explain the accumulation.
liam: can confirm: prefetch experiment set prefix entries to ttl=0 (infinite) to avoid cache churn. That was a misguided optimization for throughput.
sana: profiling details: top alloc sites show `kv_blob` pinned by cache table (hot path). Eviction runs rarely triggered because key cardinality is huge. Attached a small histogram in the CI artifact: `kv_key_cardinality: 1.2M` after 2 hours.
infra-bot: deploy-note: canary version `runtime-v3.8.1-prefetch` rolled at 1968339000, revert queued if confirmed regression.
josh: proposed quick fix: canonicalize prefix key — use a fingerprint of the prefix content only (sha1/xxhash64) + model+seqLenBucket. Drop session_id. Example:
```
string canonical_key = fmt::format("p:{}:m:{}:sl:{}", xxh64(prefix_bytes), model_name, seq_bucket);
```
this reduces cardinality and keeps session stickiness only at routing layer.
eva: I like that. Also add soft TTL (eg 6h) for prefetched prefixes and an LRU cap per-host to bound memory. TTL=0 was the culprit.
liam: tradeoffs: dropping session_id means we may lose some correctness where session-specific prompts modify the prefix shape. How often does that happen?
sana: checked diffs: ~95% of prefixes are purely input text (system prompt + few tokens). Only ~5% include session-specific ephemeral meta. For the latter we'll keep a secondary path that includes a `session_fingerprint` when the prompt contains a special marker `__SESSION_META__`.
josh: action items:
- revert ttl=0 change on canary (sana)
- implement canonical_key generation + unit tests (josh)
- add per-host LRU cap and 6h TTL for prefix cache entries (liam)
- add CI regression test for cache cardinality (eva)
sana: doing revert now and will monitor. If memory drops within 30m we mark as the regression cause and ship the key canonicalization next week.
eva: also open an infra ticket to surface `kv_key_cardinality` metric to the console (per-model, per-host). Without that we didn't notice until heap drift.
liam: noted. assign owners and let's sync in tomorrow standup. :thumbsup:
sana: thanks all — will paste memory graphs in 20m.
